Let me analyze this OIML Certificate of Conformity document.

Document details:
- Issuing Authority: Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB), Braunschweig
- Certificate No.: R76/1992-DE1-06.01, Revision 3
- Member State: Germany
- Date issued: 16.09.2013 (from signatures table)
- Person responsible: Dr. O. Mack, Head of Working Group
- Applicant: Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co. KG, Weender Landstr. 94-108, 37075 Göttingen, Germany
- Manufacturer: same as applicant ("Manufacturer of the certified type is the applicant")
- Certified type: Nonautomatic electromechanical weighing instrument with or without lever system
- Type: BD ED 100, BD ED 200 — two models
- Recommendation: R76-1, edition 1992, Amendment 1 (1994), accuracy class (I) (II)
- Test reports: 1.12-4022009 (10 pages, 3rd revision), plus associated test reports /1 (34p), /2 (137p), /3 (9p), /4 (13p), /5 (13p), /9 (20p), /10 (20p), /12 (20p). Additional info reports: /6 (11p), /7 (11p), /8 (20p), /9 (20p), /10 (20p), /11 (20p), /12 (20p).
- Page total: 3

Certificate:
- number: R76/1992-DE1-06.01
- scheme: A? This is a Type Evaluation / Conformity certificate. OIML-CS scheme A is basic, scheme B is for MAA. Standard certificates of conformity are scheme A. R76/1992 is not under MAA, so scheme: "A".
- project_number: possibly R76/1992-DE1-06.01? Or the "R3-0033" reference? Hmm, "R3-0033" appears — this might be an internal PTB reference. Actually "R3-0033" might be a revision/control number. I'll omit project_number or... The instruction says omit if not present. R3-0033 seems like an internal document number. I'll omit it.
- page_total: 3
- member_state: Germany
- date_issued: 2013-09-16
- oiml_issuer_id: not present.

Issuing authority:
- name: Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt
- address_lines: ["Bundesallee 100", "38116 Braunschweig"]
- person_responsible: Dr. O. Mack
- person_title: Head of Working Group
- oiml_issuer_id: not present

Applicants:
- Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co. KG, Weender Landstr. 94-108, 37075 Göttingen, Germany

Manufacturers: same as applicant — "Manufacturer of the certified type is the applicant". Should I include manufacturers? It says manufacturer is the applicant, so I can include the entry.

Certified type:
- category: "Weighing instrument" — The schema examples list categories like "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system"... For a nonautomatic weighing instrument, category could be "Weighing instrument" or "Nonautomatic weighing instrument". I'll use "Nonautomatic weighing instrument".
- type_designations: ["BD ED 100", "BD ED 200"]
- module_designation: null (not applicable; these are complete instruments) — omit or "Not applicable"? Not stated; omit.
- description: "Nonautomatic electromechanical weighing instrument with or without lever system. Weighing instrument with built-in display, keyboard and interface."

Model family: Two models: BD ED 100 (class I) and BD ED 200 (class II). Tables 1 and 2 give characteristics per type.

Now the characteristics. Table 1 (BD ED 100):
- Accuracy class: (I)
- Max: 50 g ... 240 g → range 50 to 240 g. Hmm, Max is a range "50 g ... 240 g" meaning Max may be chosen within limits. Value: {min: 50, max: 240}, unit g.
- e: 1 mg ... 2 mg → {min: 1, max: 2}, mg
- d: 0,1 mg ... 2 mg → {min: 0.1, max: 2}, mg
- n ≤ 240000 → max number of verification scale intervals: value 240000
- Tare-balancing range ≤ 100% of Max → value 100, unit %, reference Max? I could add tare_balancing_range with value 100, unit "%" and maybe a note. Or value "100% of Max". Rule says separate reference: value 150, unit %, and separate characteristic safe_overload_reference. I'll do value: 100, unit_symbol: "%", unit_id null, and perhaps a separate characteristic "tare_balancing_range_reference": "Max". Hmm, "Or omit if too noisy." I'll include value 100 with "%" and maybe reference. Actually simpler: value: 100, unit_symbol: "%". The "of Max" part is descriptive. I could set the value as {min:null, max:100}? No — "≤ 100% of Max" means max 100%. I'll use {min: null, max: 100}? The rule about ranges: "≤2.5m/s → value: {min: null, max: 2.5}". So ≤100% → {min: null, max: 100}. Hmm, but that's for a bounded value. "Tare-balancing range ≤ 100% of Max" → upper bound 100%. I'll do {min: null, max: 100}, unit "%". Actually the convention in the rules example: `≤2.5m/s` → `{min: null, max: 2.5}`. Follow that.

- Temperature range: "A range of 5°C up to 10°C within the limits of +15 °C up to +27 °C" — this is special temperature range for class I: a spread of 5°C to 10°C within limits +15°C to +27°C. Hmm. This is the class I special temperature range: range of 5 K up to 10 K within limits +15/+27°C. Two characteristics: temperature_range_spread: {min: 5, max: 10}, unit "°C" (actually K, delta) and temperature_range_limits: {min: 15, max: 27}, unit "°C". Hmm — how to canonicalize? Maybe:
  - temperature_range: {value: "5°C up to 10°C within the limits of +15°C up to +27°C"} — as string? The rules prefer structured. But this is complex. Alternatively:
  - `temperature_range_spread`: {min: 5, max: 10}, unit_symbol "°C"
  - `temperature_range_limits`: {min: 15, max: 27}, unit_symbol "°C"
  
  I think splitting is reasonable. But wait — for delta temperatures, unit would be K (kelvin difference), but the doc says °C. Keep °C as raw symbol.

- Nominal capacity of the load receptor: 288 g → value 288, g
- Initial zero setting + dead load ≤ 238 g (footnote 1) → value {min: null, max: 238}, g, footnote_markers ["1)"]

Footnote 1: "The sum of Max, initial zero-setting range and the dead load shall not exceed the nominal capacity of the load receptor."

Table 2 (BD ED 200):
- Accuracy class: (II)
- Max: three columns: "1 g ...620 g", "500 g ...6200 g", "5000 g ...8200 g"
- e: "0,01 g ...0,1 g", "0,1 g ...1 g", "1 g"
- d: "0,001 g ...0,1 g", "0,01 g ... 1 g", "0,1 ... 1 g"
- n ≤: 62000, 62000, 8200
- Tare-balancing range ≤: 100% of Max (all three)
- Temperature range: +10 °C / +30 °C (all three)
- Nominal capacity of load receptor: 744 g, 7440 g, 9840 g
- Initial zero setting + dead load ≤: 743 g, 6940 g, 4840 g (footnote 1)

So BD ED 200 has three weighing-range configurations. These are configurations (Max/e/d combos chosen within limits), not distinct models. Per rule 5, configuration axes: axis could be "weighing range" with three conditions.

How to model this? Options:
1. model_family models: BD ED 100, BD ED 200 (two models). Then model_level attributes: accuracy_class, and table-1 attributes for BD ED 100, table-2 attributes for BD ED 200 (where uniform across the three columns).
2. For the three weighing-range variants within BD ED 200, use config_level with axis "weighing range" (range 1, 2, 3).

Let me structure:

model_family:
- family_name: null (BD ED? Type names are BD ED 100 and BD ED 200 — family could be "BD ED". Hmm, "Type: BD ED 100, BD ED 200". The family could be "BD ED". I'd say family_name: "BD ED". That's reasonable — explicit-ish. Actually rule: "explicit family name if any, else null". "BD ED" is arguably the series name. I'll set "BD ED".)
- models:
  - model_id: "BD ED 100", label: "Table 1 — accuracy class (I)"
  - model_id: "BD ED 200", label: "Table 2 — accuracy class (II)"

characteristics.type_level (whole cert):
- "Weighing instrument with built-in display, keyboard and interface" — that's description.
- Tare-balancing range ≤ 100% of Max applies to both — could be type_level.
- Instrument category stuff.

characteristics.model_level:
- accuracy_class: BD ED 100 → "I", BD ED 200 → "II" (value string "I"/"II" — class letters; strings acceptable? Rule says numbers not strings for numbers; class is a symbol → string ok, unit null.)
- maximum_capacity (Max): BD ED 100 → {min: 50, max: 240} g; BD ED 200 → per config... hmm this is where it gets tricky. BD ED 200 has three Max ranges. So Max is config-varying for BD ED 200.

Option: Put config_level entries:
- attribute: "maximum_capacity", axis: "weighing range (BD ED 200)", values: [{condition: "Range 1", value: {min:1, max:620}, unit "g"}, {condition: "Range 2", value: {min:500, max:6200}, unit "g"}, {condition: "Range 3", value: {min:5000, max:8200}, unit "g"}]

But then BD ED 100 Max vs BD ED 200 Max — Max differs per model AND per config. I could put maximum_capacity in model_level for BD ED 100 only? That's awkward.

Alternative: treat the three BD ED 200 ranges as config axis within model_level values. The schema's model_level values are {model, value, footnote_markers} — no condition field specified, but config_level has {condition, value}. I'll follow schema: model_level for model-varying single-valued attributes; config_level for attribute × config.

Cleanest approach:
- model_level: accuracy_class (BD ED 100 → I, BD ED 200 → II).
- For BD ED 100's Max/e/d/n/nominal capacity/initial zero: these apply to a single model; put them in model_level with single value.
- For BD ED 200's three ranges: config_level with axis "weighing range" for attributes: maximum_capacity, verification_scale_interval_e, scale_interval_d, max_scale_intervals_n, nominal_capacity_load_receptor, initial_zero_setting_plus_dead_load.
- Uniform attributes: tare_balancing_range (100% Max) → type_level or model_level both models. Temperature: BD ED 100 → special (5–10 K within +15/+27), BD ED 200 → +10/+30 °C → model_level.

Let me structure:

type_level:
- tare_balancing_range: {min: null, max: 100}, "%", applies to both. Hmm, could also go to model_level with both models same. Type-level is fine since it applies to whole cert. But rule 4 says put varying attributes in model_level; uniform can be type_level. Tare is uniform → type_level.

Actually let me reconsider: put things that vary across models in model_level, uniform in type_level. 

Uniform across both models:
- tare_balancing_range ≤ 100% of Max → type_level.

Model-level (single value per model):
- accuracy_class: I / II
- maximum_capacity: BD ED 100 → {min 50, max 240} g. BD ED 200 → varies per range, so exclude from model_level and put in config_level. Hmm, but then maximum_capacity appears both in model_level (for BD ED 100) and config_level (for BD ED 200). That's messy but accurate. Alternatively, handle BD ED 200 ranges as three sub-configurations in config_level for all range-dependent attributes, and keep BD ED 100's values in model_level.

Alternatively: I could name the config conditions like "BD ED 200 — range 1 (Max 1–620 g)" etc. Let me just do:

config_level entries (axis: "weighing range of BD ED 200"):
1. attribute: maximum_capacity, unit g:
   - condition "Range 1", {min: 1, max: 620}
   - condition "Range 2", {min: 500, max: 6200}
   - condition "Range 3", {min: 5000, max: 8200}
2. attribute: verification_scale_interval_e (e), unit g:
   - Range 1: {min: 0.01, max: 0.1}
   - Range 2: {min: 0.1, max: 1}
   - Range 3: 1
3. attribute: scale_interval_d, unit g:
   - Range 1: {min: 0.001, max: 0.1}
   - Range 2: {min: 0.01, max: 1}
   - Range 3: {min: 0.1, max: 1} — note source: "0,1 ... 1 g" — d for range 3 is "0.1 ... 1 g" (0,1 ... 1 g). Yes {min 0.1, max 1}.
4. attribute: max_scale_intervals_nlc? No — this is instrument n (number of verification scale intervals), not load cell. attribute: max_verification_scale_intervals_n:
   - Range 1: 62000
   - Range 2: 62000
   - Range 3: 8200
5. attribute: nominal_capacity_of_load_receptor, unit g:
   - Range 1: 744
   - Range 2: 7440
   - Range 3: 9840
6. attribute: initial_zero_setting_plus_dead_load, unit g, footnote 1):
   - Range 1: {min: null, max: 743}
   - Range 2: {min: null, max: 6940}
   - Range 3: {min: null, max: 4840}

model_level entries:
1. accuracy_class: [{model "BD ED 100", value "I"}, {model "BD ED 200", value "II"}]
2. maximum_capacity: [{model "BD ED 100", value {min 50, max 240}, unit g}]
3. verification_scale_interval_e: [{model "BD ED 100", {min 1, max 2}, mg}]
4. scale_interval_d: [{model "BD ED 100", {min 0.1, max 2}, mg}]
5. max_verification_scale_intervals_n: [{model "BD ED 100", 240000}]
6. nominal_capacity_load_receptor: [{model "BD ED 100", 288, g}]
7. initial_zero_setting_plus_dead_load: [{model "BD ED 100", {min null, max 238}, g, footnote 1)}]
8. temperature_range: BD ED 100 → special; BD ED 200 → {min 10, max 30} °C. For BD ED 100 it's "5 K to 10 K spread within +15/+27 °C". Represent as string: "range of 5°C up to 10°C within the limits of +15°C up to +27°C". I'll set value as the string for BD ED 100, and numeric range for BD ED 200. Units: °C. Hmm, value mixed string/range — allowed since value can be number|range|string.

Also matrix_tables: should I include Table 1 and Table 2 as matrix_tables to preserve? Rule 4 for R137 example says extract as matrix_tables AND populate model_family/models and model_level. Here we have two tables. I could include them as matrix_tables with rows per range. Table 2 is naturally a matrix (3 range columns). Table 1 is single column. Including both as matrix_tables preserves data. I think including them is good:

matrix_tables:
1. name: "Table 1 — Characteristics of BD ED 100"
   columns: ["type", "accuracy_class", "maximum_capacity", "verification_scale_interval_e", "scale_interval_d", "max_verification_scale_intervals_n", "tare_balancing_range", "temperature_range", "nominal_capacity_load_receptor", "initial_zero_setting_plus_dead_load"]
   Actually the table is attribute-value pairs, not a matrix. Rows as objects: I could present as key-value: {"type": "BD ED 100", "accuracy_class": "I", ...}. Schema says rows[] object per row. For Table 1, one row object with all attributes.

Hmm, maybe simpler: two matrix_tables entries, one per table, each with rows.

Table 1:
- columns: ["attribute", "value"]? That's awkward. Better: one row with named fields.

I'll do:
Table 1:
{
  "name": "Table 1 — Weighing ranges BD ED 100",
  "columns": ["type", "accuracy_class", "maximum_capacity", "verification_scale_interval_e", "scale_interval_d", "max_verification_scale_intervals_n", "tare_balancing_range", "temperature_range", "nominal_capacity_load_receptor", "initial_zero_setting_plus_dead_load"],
  "column_units": [null, null, "g", "mg", "mg", null, "%", "°C", "g", "g"],
  "rows": [{"type": "BD ED 100", "accuracy_class": "I", "maximum_capacity": {"min": 50, "max": 240}, ...}]
}
Hmm, mixing units within rows (Max g, e mg) — column_units handles per column. OK.

Table 2:
{
  "name": "Table 2 — Weighing ranges BD ED 200",
  "columns": ["type", "accuracy_class", "maximum_capacity", "verification_scale_interval_e", "scale_interval_d", "max_verification_scale_intervals_n", "tare_balancing_range", "temperature_range", "nominal_capacity_load_receptor", "initial_zero_setting_plus_dead_load"],
  "rows": [
    {"type": "BD ED 200", "accuracy_class": "II", "maximum_capacity": {"min":1,"max":620}, "verification_scale_interval_e": {"min":0.01,"max":0.1}, "scale_interval_d": {"min":0.001,"max":0.1}, "max_verification_scale_intervals_n": 62000, "tare_balancing_range": {"min":null,"max":100}, "temperature_range": {"min":10,"max":30}, "nominal_capacity_load_receptor": 744, "initial_zero_setting_plus_dead_load": {"min":null,"max":743}},
    ... range 2, range 3
  ]
}

The schema example shows matrix_tables rows with raw numbers (qmax: 4.0) not structured value objects. So matrix_tables rows use plain values. Fine — I'll use plain numbers/ranges there and structured values in characteristics.

Footnotes: marker "1)", text "The sum of Max, initial zero-setting range and the dead load shall not exceed the nominal capacity of the load receptor."

Recommendation:
- id: "R76" (canonical: "R76" not "OIML R 76"). The doc says R76-1 (part 1). Canonical id per examples: "R60". So id: "R76". Edition: 1992. Amendment: "Amendment 1 (1994)" → maybe amendment: "1 (1994)" or "Amendment 1 (1994)". Schema: amendment (no type given). I'll use "Amendment 1 (1994)". Hmm, maybe just "1"? The doc: "R76-1, edition 1992, including Amendment 1 (1994)". I'll put amendment: "Amendment 1 (1994)". Or "1 (1994)". I'll use "Amendment 1 (1994)".
- scheme: "A" (standard OIML-CS certificate; 2013, pre-MAA for R76 presumably). Yes scheme A.
- accuracy_classes: ["I", "II"] — schema: accuracy_classes[]. Use ["I", "II"] or ["(I)", "(II)"]? Canonical: ["I", "II"].

Test reports:
- 1.12-4022009, 10 pages, 3rd revision → role: type_evaluation_report (the "Report" describing tests). id "1.12-4022009", pages 10, role type_evaluation_report. Note "(10 pages, 3rd revision)". Pages 10.
- 1.12-4022009/1, 34 pages, role test_report
- /2, 137 pages, test_report
- /3, 9 pages, test_report
- /4, 13 pages, test_report
- /5, 13 pages, test_report
- /9, 20 pages, test_report
- /10, 20 pages, test_report
- /12, 20 pages, test_report
These are "associated Test Reports". Role: test_report.

The "additional information" reports (/6, /7, /8, /9, /10, /11, /12) include merely additional information. /9, /10, /12 appear in both lists. Hmm. Role options: test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. For those with "merely additional information", maybe role "documentation_file"? The schema role enum: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. I'll assign role "test_report" for the first group and "documentation_file" for the additional-info-only ones (/6, /7, /8, /11), and for /9, /10, /12 which appear in both lists, role "test_report" (they're both test and additional info; primary classification test_report). Or mention in the entry. I'll add role "test_report" for those, since they're listed first as Test Reports.

Actually, let me list all: reports mentioned:
- Report N° 1.12-4022009 (10 pages, 3rd revision)
- Test Reports: /1 (34), /2 (137), /3 (9), /4 (13), /5 (13), /9 (20), /10 (20), /12 (20)
- Additional info: /6 (11), /7 (11), /8 (20), /9 (20), /10 (20), /11 (20), /12 (20)

I'll include entries for each unique report: base, /1../12. That's 13 entries. For /9, /10, /12 role test_report (also additional info — could add note? no notes field; skip).

Hmm, but maybe simpler to only list the first group as test_reports and mention second group too. I'll include all with roles as reasoned.

Revision history: "Revision 3" — no dates of previous revisions given. revision_history: [{revision: "3", date: "2013-09-16", changes: null}]? Changes not stated; date of this revision = issue date 16.09.2013. Rule: revision as string. I'll include {"revision": "3", "date": "2013-09-16"}. Changes omitted.

The weighing ranges with Max, Min, e, d and number of verification scale intervals may be chosen within the limits of No. 3.2 of R76-1 and of tables 1 or 2."

Also the transfer note: certificate transferred from Sartorius AG to Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co. KG. Not in schema — could note in description? Schema has no field. Skip. Applicants: the new owner. Could I mention old owner? Not in schema; omit.

model_level values need unit_symbol at attribute level per example: {"attribute": "qmax", "unit_symbol": "m³/h", "values": [...]}. Values entries: {model, value, footnote_markers}. Note unit_symbol is per-attribute, so per-model units must be same. For temperature_range: BD ED 100 string value with °C embedded; BD ED 200 numeric with unit °C. Mixed. I'll set attribute unit_symbol "°C" and value for BD ED 100 as string "spread of 5 up to 10 within limits +15 up to +27" — hmm ugly. Alternative: two model_level attributes:
- temperature_range: BD ED 200 → {min 10, max 30}
- special_temperature_range: BD ED 100 → "5°C to 10°C within +15°C to +27°C" (string).
Cleaner. I'll do that.

For config_level values: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. Schema rule 5: "Values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}." Good.

Now write the JSON.

type_level:
- tare_balancing_range: {value: {min: null, max: 100}, unit_symbol: "%", footnote_markers: []} — with reference Max. I'll include "tare_balancing_range_reference": {"value": "Max"}? Maybe include for clarity. Rule 3 example does that for 150% of Emax. I'll include tare_balancing_range: {min null, max 100}, "%" and skip separate reference... The rule says "(Or omit if too noisy.)" for the reference. I'll include the reference as a separate type_level characteristic "tare_balancing_range_reference": {"value": "Max"}. Fine.

Also maybe "verification_scale_intervals_choosable": description covers it. Skip.

Model family models: include attributes? Schema: models[]: model_id, label, attributes{}. I can put label "Accuracy class (I)" etc. Keep attributes minimal since model_level holds them.

Let me now also double-check Table 1 temperature: "A range of 5°C up to 10°C within the limits of +15 °C up to +27 °C". This is class I special temperature: a temperature range spread of 5 K up to 10 K within limits +15°C to +27°C. Represent: value: "A range of 5°C up to 10°C within the limits of +15°C up to +27°C". As string (formulas/symbols keep as string). I'll normalize comma decimals etc. Fine.

Table 2 temperature: "+10 °C / +30 °C" → {min: 10, max: 30}, °C.

n ≤ values: 240000; 62000; 62000; 8200.

Initial zero setting + dead load: footnote marker 1) applies.

Now attribute naming:
- maximum_capacity (Max)
- verification_scale_interval_e

- tare_balancing_range
- temperature_range

- accuracy_class

config_level axis: "weighing range (BD ED 200)". Conditions: "Range 1", "Range 2", "Range 3". Maybe more descriptive: "BD ED 200 — Range 1 (Max 1–620 g)". Keep "Range 1" simple with description in axis.

Let me also reconsider whether the three columns of Table 2 should instead be three models (BD ED 200 range variants). The type designation is "BD ED 200" for all three; they're one instrument with selectable weighing ranges. So config axis is right.

matrix_tables column_units for Table 1: max g; e mg; d mg; n dimensionless; tare %; temp °C; nominal capacity g; initial zero g. Table 2 same but e/d in g.

For matrix_tables rows, temperature_range for BD ED 100 is a string; fine.

Table 2 rows:
Row1: max {min 1, max 620}; e {0.01, 0.1}; d {0.001, 0.1}; n 62000; tare 100 (% — as number 100 with unit in column_units); temp {10, 30}; capacity 744; initial zero 743.
Row2: max {500, 6200}; e {0.1, 1}; d {0.01, 1}; n 62000; temp same; capacity 7440; iz 6940.
Row3: max {5000, 8200}; e 1; d {0.1, 1}; n 8200; capacity 9840; iz 4840.

For matrix rows tare: 100 (unit %). I'll just put 100.

Test report list — dates not given for individual reports; only the cert date. Omit date.

role for base report: "type_evaluation_report". Wait — the base is "the Report N° 1.12-4022009 (10 pages, 3rd revision)" — tests described in the Report. It's the type evaluation report. role: "type_evaluation_report". pages: 10.
